data.content_ref: inline:The target's mechanism asserts that 'Choosing the one that hasn't failed yet is the only rational move available.' This is a false uniqueness claim. The target's own disanalogies concede that biological survival is 'non-normative and retrospective' while scientific preference is 'prospective and normative,' establishing an is-ought gap: mere past survival of a theory cannot, by the target's own logic, entail that one OUGHT to prefer it. Yet the mechanism leaps from 'we know which theories have failed' to the normative conclusion that preferring the non-failed theory is 'the only rational move.' This ignores rationally available alternatives — suspending judgment, methodological pluralism (pursuing multiple surviving theories simultaneously), or treating corroboration as instrumentally useful without committing to preference — none of which require induction. The target thus smuggles a normative premise (one ought to prefer survivors) through an analogy whose own stated disanalogies show cannot support it, rendering the 'defense' circular: it defends preference by assuming preference is the only option, which is precisely what needed defending.
